Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are out on the field and so is the fielding team who have taken their respective positions. Will Young and Finn Allen will open the batting innings while Shoriful Islam has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, an entertaining bowling performance by New Zealand in the first innings made sure that they have to chase only 172 runs on the board in 50 overs. It was possible due to an all-round bowling attack and some good captaincy from Lockie Ferguson. It is now up to the batters to chase the target while Bangladesh try to stop them with their bowling attack. Who do you think will win? We will find out soon as we bring you the live coverage of the run chase in a short while. Grab a cup of coffee and sit tight till then.

Trent Boult is in for a chat. He starts by crediting the guys for the way they bowled. Mentions that Bangladesh came out with a positive intent but the bowlers stuck at it. Reckons that they will have to bat well and they cannot take the total lightly. Shares that the wicket was slow and it was important to adapt. Feels that this is a good learning for them ahead of the World Cup.

What a superb bowling performance by the Kiwis. Adam Milne struck early on in the innings followed by Trent Boult who has a habit of taking wickets in the first few overs. This deadly pace duo bruised the opposition badly in the first 8 overs taking the wickets of their three main batters. In the middle phases just as Mushfiqur Rahim and Najmul Hossain Shanto were building a strong partnership, the skipper, Lockie Ferguson used his pace and dismissed the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim. The next batter to get set on the pitch was Mahmudullah who was sent back to the pavilion by Adam Milne. The Kiwis knew that until Najmul Hossain Shanto was on the crease, the runs would keep coming. Cole McConchie weaved his spin magic to dismiss the opposition's skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and sealed the innings for them. After his dismissal, none of the batters could score runs and New Zealand managed to bowl them out for 171 runs. Adam Milne was the star of the day as he finished with career-best figures of 4-34.

Bangladesh won the toss and chose to bat first. They felt that the dry wicket would help them put up a good total on the board. Safe to say that the call did not go their way. Their openers, Tanzid Hasan and Zakir Hasan were dismissed very early on in the innings putting pressure on the middle order. The stand-in skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto took the reigns into his own hands and took apart the Kiwi bowlers. The only problem was that wickets kept falling at the other end. Towhid Hridoy fell after a brief stand followed by the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim. Mahmudullah put up a good partnership but he too was sent back before he could build his innings. After that Bangladesh was never in the innings as Najmul Hossain Shanto also came under pressure and was eventually dismissed. A poor batting performance from the hosts and they have managed to put only a 171 runs on the board.

What a brilliant bowling performance from the Black Caps. They have bowled out Bangladesh for 171 runs. Adam Milne was the pick of the bowlers as he scalped 4 wickets with Trent Boult picking up a couple as well. A pretty neat performance from the bowlers.

Skies it high in the air towards extra cover where Will Young settles under it and does the rest.

Commentary.Commentary: On length and outside off with a hint of outswing. Najmul Hossain Shanto opts not to play this one and lets it go to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Adam Milne to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on off. Najmul Hossain Shanto drives it to deep cover for a couple of runs to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Adam Milne to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto walks in now.

OUT! TIMBER! Adam Milne has drawn first blood and it is the debutant Zakir Hasan that has to depart. Adam Milne bowls a perfect yorker early on in the innings straight on the off pole. The left-hander tried to take it on the full but missed the line completely. The ball smashes into the off stump and New Zealand have their first breakthrough. What a ball by Adam Milne.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Adam Milne to Zakir Hasan, OUT! b Adam Milne.

Commentary.Commentary: Full now on the off pole. Zakir Hasan drives it back to Adam Milne.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Adam Milne to Zakir Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A good start from Adam Milne. He bowls this on length and swings in onto the pads. Zakir Hasan tries to flick it but the ball hits his pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Adam Milne to Zakir Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Adam Milne will steam in from the other end.
Fuller again this time on leg. Zakir Hasan flicks it away to fine leg for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Trent Boult to Zakir Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Trent Boult goes full now on off. Zakir Hasan blocks it on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Trent Boult to Zakir Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the hard length and on off. Tanzid Hasan slaps it to cover and takes a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Trent Boult to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Tanzid Hasan is off the mark in style! Trent Boult bowls this on length and on middle. Tanzid Hasan punches it down the ground this time to the left of Boult. The ball runs away for a boundary to start off the innings.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Trent Boult to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Same length and over off an middle. Tanzid Hasan drives it down the ground and Trent Boult makes a good diving stop to his right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Trent Boult to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lovely start from Trent Boult! He bowls this on length and nips back in onto the thigh pads. Tanzid Hasan tries to block it as the ball rolls away from his pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Trent Boult to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to commence. The two umpires make their way out to the middle. The New Zealand players are in a huddle before they disperse. Loud cheers from the crowd as the two Bangladesh openers, Tanzid Hasan and Zakir Hasan stride out to the centre. Trent Boult will start the proceedings with the new ball for New Zealand. Off we go...

UPDATE - 1:42 pm IST (8:12 am GMT) - Some good visuals from the ground as all the covers have come off and the rain has stopped. The umpires are on the field to check the conditions and it looks like we will get to see the start of the match soon. Fingers crossed!

UPDATE - 1:31 pm IST (8:01 am GMT) - Uh oh! This is certainly not the way any of us would have wanted to start our day with. The covers are on at the moment as it is raining. It is only a light drizzle and therefore, only the square has been covered for now. The ground staff are lurking near the covers and let's hope that the rain subsides soon. Stay tuned for more updates.

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman is pitchside. He says that there was extra bounce and extra movement off the seam in the previous game. Mentions that this is a different surface with dry grass. Feels that the ball will skid on and reckons that there will be spin later.

New Zealand's captain Lockie Ferguson says that they would have batted first as well. Mentions that it was a challenging time to bat in the last game and hopes to make early inroads here. Informs that Kyle Jamieson is out and Adam Milne comes in for him. Also informs that Dean Foxcroft is making his ODI debut and he is replacing Chad Bowes.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper of Bangladesh, says that they will bat first. Feels that it is a dry wicket and will look to put runs on the board. Mentions that they want to enjoy and win this game. Informs that there are four changes in the side with Mushfiqur Rahim returning to the side. Reckons that the first 10 overs are important.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Will Young, Dean Foxcroft (On ODI Debut) (In for Chad Bowes), Henry Nicholls, Tom Blundell (WK), Rachin Ravindra, Cole McConchie, Adam Milne (In for Kyle Jamieson), Ish Sodhi, Lockie Ferguson (C), Trent Boult.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Najmul Hossain Shanto (C) (In for Tamim Iqbal), Tanzid Hasan, Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK) (In for Soumya Sarkar), Zakir Hasan (On ODI Debut) (In for Litton Das), Mahedi Hasan, Nasum Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Khaled Ahmed (In for Mustafizur Rahman), Shoriful Islam.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of Bangladesh. They have elected to BAT first.

New Zealand, on the other hand, will be coming into this match on a positive note. They clinched a comfortable victory in sub-continental conditions which will be a big help ahead of their World Cup campaign. They had a good outing in the 2nd ODI as some good partnerships made sure the team crossed the 250-run mark. Their bowling unit complemented the batters well and maintained the pressure on their opponents throughout the 2nd innings and prevented them from successfully chasing their score. A win in this match would clinch the series for the Kiwis and that will be a great boost for their confidence. With the World Cup just around the corner, this series is a very important one for both teams as they will test their squads for the conditions and type of pitches found in India. They will hope to collect a lot of insights from this 3-ODI series and the winner of the series will gain some much needed momentum. This is expected to be a very exciting clash. The weather looks great and live action will take center stage shortly. Stay with us as we bring you the toss and team news soon.

The hosts, Bangladesh are currently in the losing end of the series as they lost the last ODI. The first match was washed out but their opponents clinched a good win over them in the 2nd ODI. This is the last chance for the hosts to win the match and tie the series. In the last match, their bowlers did well to restrict the visitors to a chaseable target and took timely wickets. The batters let them down. Barring a few good partnerships, none of the batters could take the innings deep and ended up being bowled out by their opposition. They will hope the batting unit finds its form back in this final ODI, especially Towhid Hridoy, and Najmul Hossain Shanto.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. We are in the capital city of Bangladesh, Dhaka for the third and final ODI between Bangladesh and New Zealand. This is the last ODI both teams will play ahead of the 2023 World Cup.

The cricketing world braces itself for the culmination of an interesting ODI series between Bangladesh and New Zealand, with the Kiwis currently holding a 1-0 lead. The series has seen its fair share of twists, with the first ODI being washed out and New Zealand securing a commanding win in the second encounter. The third and final ODI is scheduled to unfold at the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur, where the weather forecast hints at partly cloudy skies, albeit with a chance of rain showers. The outcome of this series hinges on this crucial match, and cricket enthusiasts remain hopeful of witnessing a full game despite the unpredictable weather. Bangladesh's ODI record against New Zealand may not inspire overwhelming confidence, with the Tigers having faced the Kiwis 39 times since 1990, managing to secure victory on only 10 occasions. Despite a commendable performance by their spinners in the second ODI, where they dismissed New Zealand for 254 runs, Bangladesh's batting struggles in the middle order remain a glaring concern, a predicament that has persisted since their outing in the Asia Cup. In the previous match, Bangladesh capitulated for a mere 168 runs, succumbing to an 86-run defeat, with leg-spinner Ish Sodhi wreaking havoc by claiming six wickets for New Zealand. As Bangladesh seeks to address their batting woes, particularly in the middle order, the top-order batsmen must shoulder the responsibility of accumulating substantial runs, setting the tone for the upcoming World Cup. Meanwhile, New Zealand aims to secure a series victory, eager to rebound following their defeat against England. As the stakes run high in this pivotal third ODI, cricket aficionados worldwide anxiously await the outcome, fervently hoping that inclement weather does not disrupt the proceedings, enabling us to determine the victor of this riveting series.
